patients.summary: Data entry specialist who joins the practice at 35 with autoimmune hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 88 mcg. Gynecology later diagnoses primary ovarian insufficiency during an infertility evaluation, orthopedics diagnoses right carpal tunnel syndrome, and depression diagnosed in 2024 goes on to a slow, disappointing sertraline course with psychiatry.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 35 y/o woman looking for a new primary care doctor after her previous office stopped taking new appointments for months out. Explained the membership model and what insurance still covers. She wants to go ahead. Booked new patient visit for 9/14 at 9:00. Records release faxed to her prior primary care office today. She takes one thyroid pill, will bring the bottle.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

Dawn is a 35-year-old data entry specialist transferring care from another primary care office. No acute concerns today; she mostly wants someone she can reach.

History: Hypothyroidism diagnosed around 2014 at her old office, told it was autoimmune. Dose was adjusted a few times early on and has been levothyroxine 88 mcg every morning for years, TSH reportedly fine on it. Takes it on an empty stomach, coffee about 45 minutes later. No palpitations, heat or cold intolerance, change in bowel habits, hair or skin change.
Gyn: menses regular, about every 28 days, no heavy bleeding. Not using hormonal contraception. Last Pap at old office, she thinks 2019, normal.
No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. No supplements.
Allergies: none known to medications.
Family: mother has major depression. A maternal aunt has hypothyroid and went through menopause very early, around 34. Paternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis.
Social: married, lives with husband. Works full time doing data entry, mostly at a keyboard. Never smoker. A drink once or twice a month at most. No drug use. Walks, likes to cook.

ROS: negative except as above. Mood good. Sleeping fine.

Exam: Well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules palpated. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash. Neuro grossly intact.
PHQ-9: 3.

Assessment and plan:
1. Hypothyroidism, autoimmune - stable by history. Continue levothyroxine 88 mcg. TSH today.
2. Health maintenance - baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. HIV and hep C screening once, she agrees. Requested old records for Pap date and vaccines. Flu shot next month when this year's supply comes in; she will book a nurse visit.

Follow up: annual physical in the spring, sooner as needed. Gave her the practice cell number for texts.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dawn, all of your labs from Tuesday came back normal. Thyroid level is right where it should be on the 88 mcg, so no change. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests and cholesterol all look good. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative, and those don't need repeating unless something changes. Talk soon.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Prior primary care office, records released at patient request. 41 pages.

Summary of contents:
- Problem list: hypothyroidism, autoimmune thyroiditis. Diagnosed May 2014 when a screening TSH came back high; thyroid peroxidase antibodies positive at that time. Levothyroxine started and titrated over 2014-2015 to 88 mcg daily, unchanged since. Annual TSH values on file all within range on that dose.
- Medications: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical screening: Pap with HPV co-test 06/2019, negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV negative.
- Immunizations: Tdap 06/2017. COVID-19 Moderna dose 1 03/2021, dose 2 04/2021 (patient-provided card copy). Influenza most years.
- No surgical history. No hospitalizations.

Filed to chart. Immunizations entered. Next Pap due 2024.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here before work for flu vaccine. Feeling well, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM given in left upper arm. VIS reviewed. Sat for 15 minutes, no reaction. She'll keep an eye out for COVID booster eligibility.

documents.title: Levothyroxine refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request from patient's pharmacy for levothyroxine 88 mcg, #90. TSH normal 9/2021. Routed to PCP and approved with 3 refills.

documents.title: Got my booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know I got my COVID booster on Saturday at the pharmacy near work. It was the Pfizer one. Arm was sore for a day, that's it. Do you need a picture of the card?

documents.title: RE: Got my booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Dawn! No picture needed, the pharmacy record came through and we've added the 1/8/22 booster to your chart.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Doing well. Busy stretch at work, long days on the computer but no complaints about hands, neck or eyes. Takes levothyroxine faithfully. Periods regular. Sleeps ok. Mood good.
Meds: levothyroxine 88 mcg daily. NKDA.
Social unchanged: never smoker, rare alcohol.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: NAD. Vitals reviewed. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, thyroid normal size and nontender. CV regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs CTA. Abdomen benign. Extremities warm, no swelling. Skin: no concerning lesions.

Impression:
- Healthy 35 y/o. Hypothyroidism stable, recheck TSH, refills sent.
- Pap/HPV last 2019, due 2024.
- Vaccines: Tdap good until 2027. Flu in the fall.
- Cholesterol normal last fall; no need to repeat this year.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Thyroid result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Dawn - TSH is normal again. Keep the same dose. See you next spring, and text if anything comes up before then.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: After-work vaccine appointment. Afebrile, feels well. Quadrivalent influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer bivalent COVID booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. VIS for both given. Observed 15 min, tolerated well, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Levothyroxine 90-day supply
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: levothyroxine 88 mcg, refills exhausted. Last TSH 4/2022 normal. Approved per standing protocol, #90 x 3. Pharmacy notes manufacturer change on the generic; let patient know via portal that the strength and dose are the same.
